extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and editors (AP subscribers)
extracted.subtask_description: Associated Press wire copy covering Korean War developments, wartime press restrictions, military and logistical policies, and related governmental and scientific statements; includes operational guidance for news coverage and specifications for military supplies. Useful for journalists, editors, and policy observers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chicago Sun-Times self-censorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: For the duration of the emergency, the Sun-Times will not report the departure of troops from American ports, the names or nature of the transports or other vessels on which they are moving, or the ports of destination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule will apply also to photographs that would reveal similar information. The only exception to this rule will be official announcements which, in our opinion, will not endanger American lives. Rationale given: 'to safeguard the lives' of Americans in present or potential danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Defense restriction on release of troop/supply movement information
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary of Defense Johnson issued instructions to military officers restricting the issuance of information on the movement of troops and supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until those instructions, there was no uniform policy on what officers could release to the press. The guidance is procedural (restrict issuance) and intended to prevent operational details (e.g., names of ships, cargo) from being disclosed during wartime operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid alarmist war reporting / align tone with official communiqués
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that press and radio coverage of the Korean War has been 'alarmist' and that many news stories and newscasts give impressions exceeding official casualty reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Former newspaperman Rep. Hagen suggested war correspondents and their publications 'cease being alarmists.' Official communiqués indicate casualties are 'deplorable' but 'fall far short of what one might expect after reading many of the news stories.' Implicit evaluative criterion for reporting: avoid sensationalizing casualty figures and maintain proportion with verified official reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated Press wartime coverage standards (assignment & content)
rubrics_metrics.description: AP is expanding staff operations to assure intensive news and picture coverage of the Korean story; reinforcements and veteran correspondents are being assigned to frontline and sensitive areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance includes: assign experienced frontline reporters (e.g., Boyle, Whitehead, Morin, Lambert); deploy extra staff to Korean front and Tokyo; offer interpretive and analytical columns and background stories; produce and distribute spot maps and coordinated picture relay; coordinate plane connections and logistical support to ensure timely dispatches and photos. Emphasis on firsthand, hazardous-condition reporting and interpretive/analytical context for the biggest story since WWII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assault food packet (new field ration) specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The new 'assault food packet' replacing the K ration contains canned meats (eight kinds), crackers, a cookie, a piece of chocolate, cigarettes, matches, toilet paper, and powdered milk; canned 'bread' (cake) that can be readied in one minute is also distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and performance requirements: produce palatable, nourishing food which will stand up to two years' storage; not melt in hot climates; be edible to troops in freezing climates; be strong enough to withstand bumps and jolts of thousands of miles of transportation. Milk fat shipped to forward areas for recombining; powdered milk formulated to 'more nearly approach cow milk' than previous army products. Rationale includes morale value and logistical durability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for price support under national planting allotments (wheat policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: To achieve the government's wheat production goal, a national planting allotment was set and will be apportioned among individual farmers; growers will be free to plant in excess of allotments, but only those who remain within allotments will be eligible for price support aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agriculture Department set a national planting allotment (figures provided) to reach a target crop; remaining within allotted acreage is an explicit eligibility criterion for receiving price support (averaging $1.99 a bushel this year). This is both an allocation and an incentive/enforcement mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design criteria for prototype atomic power unit for large ships
rubrics_metrics.description: A private engineering firm was commissioned to design a prototype of an atomic power unit for large ships that is small enough to be feasible in a ship, yet practical in operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of the prototype study is to enable the government to decide whether the time is ripe to put an atomic power unit in a ship for a practical test. Implicit design demands: compactness, operational practicality, and suitability for maritime deployment. Ministry of Supply declined to elaborate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria/demands for Soviet information on German POWs (British note to Moscow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Britain formally requested Moscow to admit an international commission to investigate claims that only 13,546 German prisoners remain, and demanded that Russia: 1) identify and give the whereabouts of the prisoners admittedly still being held; 2) permit the prisoners to correspond with their families; 3) 'give full details of any persons whom the Soviet government, by classification as civilian workers or in any other way, have deprived of prisoner of war status and have thereby excluded from their prisoner of war statistics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit procedural and transparency criteria Britain requires of Soviet repatriation claims; failure to provide such information is characterized as violating principles of common humanity and prior agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radioactive waste disposal feasibility criteria (atomic energy conference commentary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ocean dilution of radioactive effluent is not a viable solution to disposal; alternative is concentration and storage in remote regions since dilution does not reduce significant radioactive content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers argued that even the Atlantic Ocean would not be big enough for disposal if substantial nuclear energy use occurred. Feasible disposal would require concentration and storage because dispersion/dilution is insufficient; quantities involved and engineering challenges must be considered. This frames criteria for acceptable waste-disposal methods.
